source.episode_title: Barabbas Means Son of the Father
source.anchor_kjv: Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them, Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?
source.thread: The prisoner set free carries the name son of the father; Jesus, the true Son of the Father, is sent to the cross
source.hook_line: # Barabbas: Son of the Father — Matthew 27:15-26 Series: Words from the Cross · Cluster 1 (The Cross) · style: animated manga grids · 40s short Note: KJV quotes
source.spoken_script: # Barabbas: Son of the Father — Matthew 27:15-26 Series: Words from the Cross · Cluster 1 (The Cross) · style: animated manga grids · 40s short Note: KJV quotes are short clause-level partials, tagged on screen — Matthew 27:17 (Pilate), 27:21 (crowd), 27:23 (Pilate), 27:22 (crowd). "Abba" is Mark 14:36. "Bar-abbas" means "son of the father". Matthew 27:25 is not used. Words LOCKED 2026-11-09. [narrator] "Barabbas" means "son of the father." [narrator] He was a robber in prison. [narrator] Pilate, the governor, offered to free one man. He knew the leaders were jealous of Jesus. [pilate] Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ? [crowd] Barabbas. [pilate] Why, what evil hath he done? [crowd] Let him be crucified. [narrator] Listen: Bar-ABBA. Jesus called God "Abba." It means Father. [narrator] So the robber went free. The true Son of the Father did not. [narrator] Barabbas was born with that name. Jesus died to give it to us.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

Minor notes, none blocking:
- youtube_short / facebook title and description: "Barabbas means 'son of the father'" is the standard reading of Bar-abbas, stated as plain fact. A few scholars read "son of the teacher". Acceptable for a short; keep it as "means", never "proves".
- All platforms: the quoted anchor (Matthew 27:17 "Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus which is called Christ?") matches the KJV verbatim. The range line (27:17, 21, 22, 23) matches what the film quotes. "Robber" is correctly credited to John 18:40 and "Abba" to Mark 14:36.
- The film's last line ("Jesus died to give it to us") rests on Romans 8:15 and Galatians 4:5-6, which are not cited in the copy. If asked in comments, answer with those verses; do not add them to titles.
- No fear or gain/loss framing, no people group blamed, Matthew 27:25 not used. The hook delivers what the film shows.
- TikTok / Instagram: the first line is the hook; fine for the platform.
